aspects.says: An ISOException that escapes is logged with its stack trace in one central handler and turned into a plain error answer.
aspects.reason: the handler is Spring MVC controller advice, which a graded run does not have; its content is one log call

aspects.says: An ISO-8583 project is split into packages by responsibility: configuration, channels, packagers, participants, services and utilities.
aspects.reason: a directory layout is a convention to follow, not behaviour a graded run can check

aspects.says: A debugging participant writes a line to the transaction's context at prepare, commit and abort, so a trace shows how far each transaction went.
aspects.reason: the participant lifecycle is the transaction manager's subject; here it only carries a log line, which the logging exercise already practises

aspects.says: Performance comes from reusing work: a tuned packager, a pool of connections instead of one per message, and a cache for results read again and again.
aspects.reason: the examples are empty packager overrides, a pool factory that is not a jPOS class and needs a live peer, and Spring cache configuration; none has a behaviour to check offline

aspects.says: Transaction processing and channel management live in separate classes, each handed what it needs rather than building it.
aspects.reason: the example is Spring wiring around an empty method and a live ISOServer; there is no behaviour of its own to practise

aspects.says: A jPOS LogListener sees every event the logger delivers, picks out the transaction events by their tag, and hands every event on so the listeners after it still see it.
